reasons: Lake identity gives case_name United States v. August, court U.S. Court of Appeals, 5th Circuit, date_decided 2025-05-08, year 2025, and docket 24-30457.
Lake official citation is 136 F.4th 595, matching the asserted reporter citation; the content page displays the full cite as 136 F.4th 595 (5th Cir. 2025).
The opinion centers on warrantless protective sweeps of August's backyard and home for officer safety while officers investigated gunfire and awaited a warrant.
The decision is dated 2025-05-08 and affirmed denial of suppression based on those protective sweeps, so the Securing the Scene home role as a recent development is supported.
residual_risks: The disclosed files do not separately define the corpus taxonomy for Securing the Scene, so this is verified from the ordinary meaning of the role and the page context.

defect.evidence_quote: It makes no difference that officers chose to investigate these concerns only after arresting August.
defect.locator_note: content_page.md frontmatter holding; compare text slip pages 5, 7, and 10.
defect.problem: The holding overstates the case as a broad doctrinal extension of Buie's officer-safety rationale. The opinion states and applies the established Mendez four-part test; the non-arrest point is supported for the backyard/curtilage sweep, while the home sweep was analyzed after August was arrested.
defect.proposed_fix: Recast as: Applies the Fifth Circuit's established Mendez four-part protective-sweep test, including its curtilage formulation, and holds on these facts that the pre-arrest backyard sweep and later home sweep were lawful based on articulable officer-safety concerns.

reasons: The four-part protective-sweep test is present in the opinion, but the court introduces it as the existing Mendez test rather than a new August articulation.
The curtilage/backyard application is supported: the opinion says August was not arrested until after officers concluded the yard sweep.

The home-sweep discussion invokes Buie after arresting August, so the asserted non-arrest/investigatory-entry language should be limited to the backyard/curtilage sweep and not stated as a broader rule.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Limit the proposition to application of the established Mendez test to curtilage and to the facts of the pre-arrest backyard sweep, instead of saying August broadly extends Buie to investigatory entries.
